claims.claim_text: Bell's major U.S. Government programs are for the production and support of V-22 tiltrotor aircraft (primarily for DoD); Bell continues to receive production, upgrade and support orders for V-22, but expects these programs to represent a lower portion of Bell's military revenue in the future (final V-22 deliveries expected in next two years, transitioning to support stage).
claims.subject: Bell V-22 tiltrotor
claims.predicate: named-program revenue from DoD; transitioning from production to sustainment
claims.object_value: material portion of Bell military revenue (Bell military aircraft revenue $1,701M in 2023)
claims.source_quote: Under current contracts, production of the V-22 tiltrotor aircraft is expected to end with final deliveries in the next two years after which this program will transition to the support stage.

claims.claim_text: Bell is the prime contractor on the U.S. Army's Future Long Range Assault Aircraft (FLRAA) program, awarded December 2022, developing a tiltrotor based on the V-280 Valor. The FLRAA program has begun to represent an increasing portion of Bell's military aircraft and support program revenues; Bell expects FLRAA to become a primary multi-decade revenue driver as it transitions from EMD to production.
claims.subject: Bell FLRAA / V-280 Valor (Future Long Range Assault Aircraft, Army FVL initiative)
claims.predicate: prime contractor, EMD ramping, expected to grow into production
claims.object_value: increasing portion of Bell military revenue; rev growth driver post-2024
claims.source_quote: The FLRAA development contract was awarded to Bell in December 2022 as part of the U.S. Army's Future Vertical Lift (FVL) initiative... The FLRAA program has begun to represent an increasing portion of Bell's revenues as development activities have ramped.

claims.claim_text: Bell continues to develop the Bell 360 Invictus for the U.S. Army's Future Attack Reconnaissance Aircraft (FARA) Competitive Prototype Program; however, on February 8, 2024 the U.S. Army announced plans to discontinue development of FARA at the conclusion of FY24 prototyping activities (disclosed as subsequent event in the FY2023 10-K). In Q1 2024 the Shadow and FARA programs were cancelled, resulting in additional severance costs under the restructuring plan.
claims.subject: Bell 360 Invictus / FARA program
claims.predicate: program-of-record discontinued by Army on 2024-02-08; cancellation costs already booked in Q1 2024 restructuring
claims.source_quote: On February 8, 2024, as part of plans to rebalance its aviation modernization investments, the U.S. Army announced plans to discontinue development of the FARA at the conclusion of FY24 prototyping activities... In the first quarter of 2024, both the Shadow and Future Attack Reconnaissance Aircraft programs were cancelled at the Textron Systems and Bell segments, resulting in additional severance costs under the restructuring plan.

claims.claim_text: Bell produces H-1 helicopters (AH-1Z / UH-1Y) for the U.S. Marine Corps; final deliveries under the current USMC contract are expected in early 2024, transitioning the platform fully to the support stage. In Q1 2024 Bell received a foreign military sale award for 12 AH-1Z helicopters (FMS continuation).
claims.subject: Bell H-1 (AH-1Z / UH-1Y) Marine Corps program
claims.predicate: USMC production line ending early 2024, transitioning to sustainment; FMS-only future demand
claims.object_value: Bell military revenue at risk of step-down absent FLRAA + FMS bridge
claims.source_quote: For the H-1 helicopter, final deliveries under the current contract are expected to be completed in early 2024, fully transitioning this platform to the support stage.

claims.claim_text: Shadow is named as the U.S. Army's premier tactical unmanned aircraft system, a notable product produced by the Textron Systems segment. (In Q1 2024 the Shadow program was cancelled, leading to severance / restructuring; the FTUAS competition replaced Shadow as the Army's tactical UAS program of record.)
claims.subject: Textron Systems Shadow tactical UAS (RQ-7) / FTUAS replacement
claims.predicate: Army cancelled Shadow program in Q1 2024; FTUAS competition awarded to another vendor
claims.object_value: Textron Systems weapons/UAS revenue line at risk; FTUAS pivot incomplete
claims.source_quote: Notable products developed and produced by the Textron Systems segment include... Shadow, the U.S. Army's premier tactical unmanned aircraft system... In the first quarter of 2024, both the Shadow and Future Attack Reconnaissance Aircraft programs were cancelled at the Textron Systems and Bell segments.

claims.claim_text: Textron Systems produces the Aerosonde Small Unmanned Aircraft System, a multi-mission capable UAS for commercial and military operations; it is also a candidate / participant in U.S. Navy / Army fee-for-service UAS programs.
claims.subject: Textron Systems Aerosonde SUAS
claims.object_value: fee-for-service UAS revenue stream within Textron Systems
claims.source_quote: the Aerosonde Small Unmanned Aircraft System, a multi-mission capable unmanned aircraft system for commercial and military operations.

claims.claim_text: Textron Systems is the prime contractor on the U.S. Navy's Ship-to-Shore Connector (SSC, LCAC-100 class), the next-generation Landing Craft Air Cushion vehicle; described as a 'notable product' of the segment with multi-year deliveries.
claims.subject: Textron Systems Ship-to-Shore Connector / LCAC-100 program
claims.predicate: USN prime contractor; multi-year production program
claims.object_value: material Textron Systems Marine & Land Systems revenue ($1.4B+ obligated history)
claims.source_quote: Notable products developed and produced by the Textron Systems segment include the Ship-to-Shore Connector, the U.S. Navy's next generation of Landing Craft Air Cushion vehicles.

claims.claim_text: Approximately 21% of Textron's 2023 revenues (~$2.87B of $13.7B) were derived from sales to U.S. Government entities, principally under DoD defense-related programs (Bell V-22/H-1/FLRAA, Textron Systems Shadow/SSC/UAS, Textron Aviation T-6/AT-6 trainers, ATAC red-air services).
claims.subject: Textron consolidated DoD revenue concentration
claims.source_quote: During 2023, we derived approximately 21% of our revenues from sales to a variety of U.S. Government entities. Our revenues from the U.S. Government largely result from contracts awarded to us under various U.S. Government defense-related programs.

claims.claim_text: Textron Aviation's military trainer and defense aircraft include the Beechcraft T-6 trainer (used to train pilots from more than 40 countries) and the AT-6 light attack military aircraft.
claims.subject: Textron Aviation T-6 / AT-6 trainer program
claims.predicate: FMS-driven trainer and light attack aircraft, USAF certified
claims.object_value: trainer + AT-6 revenue line within Textron Aviation aircraft
claims.source_quote: Textron Aviation's military trainer and defense aircraft include the Beechcraft T-6 trainer, which has been used to train pilots from more than 40 countries, and the AT-6 light attack military aircraft, which has achieved military type certification from the U.S. Air Force.

claims.claim_text: Airborne Tactical Advantage Company (ATAC), part of Textron Systems, provides live military air-to-air and air-to-ship training and adversary 'red air' support services for U.S. Navy, Marine, and Air Force personnel.
claims.subject: ATAC red-air contract adversary air services
claims.object_value: Textron Systems services revenue (~$208M USAspending history)
claims.source_quote: live military air-to-air and air-to-ship training and support services for U.S. Navy, Marine and Air Force personnel provided by Airborne Tactical Advantage Company.

claims.claim_text: Textron Aviation backlog at the end of 2023 was $7,169M; Bell backlog was $4,780M; Textron Systems backlog was $1,950M (total backlog $13,899M); approximately 21% of 2023 revenues were from U.S. Government customers.
